title: Fragmented ETF Relative Strength
market_niche: Sector, factor, and asset-class ETFs where leadership rotates across fragmented investor mandates.
phenomenon: Relative strength may persist when capital reallocates gradually across asset classes, sectors, or styles.
counterparty_or_forced_actor: Mandate-bound allocators, benchmark-aware managers, model portfolios, and slow-moving retirement or advisory flows.
why_edge_might_exist: Portfolio reallocations often happen incrementally, so relative leadership can persist longer than one rebalance period.
why_large_funds_might_ignore_it: The liquid ETF version is well known and likely crowded; smaller niche ETFs may have limited capacity, wider spreads, and operational overhead.

institutional_constraint_evidence.expected_daily_dollar_volume: high for broad ETFs, variable for niche ETFs
institutional_constraint_evidence.estimated_position_size: unknown until the ETF universe is fixed
institutional_constraint_evidence.estimated_strategy_capacity: likely high in broad ETFs and lower in niche ETFs

expected_capacity: High for broad liquid ETFs, but the most interesting small-capital version may require less-liquid niche ETFs.
persistence_mechanism: Mandate changes, risk-budget shifts, and model-portfolio reallocations may create slow-moving flow pressure.
crowding_risk: High in broad ETF momentum; lower only if the universe is fragmented enough and costs are modeled honestly.
edge_decay_trigger: The thesis weakens if relative-strength winners fail across walk-forward windows or only work in one asset universe after tuning.
observable_prediction: A prespecified relative-strength rotation should improve risk-adjusted return versus a static benchmark without excessive turnover.
falsification_tests: Reject if walk-forward validation fails out of sample.
Reject if results depend on one tuned lookback or one cherry-picked universe.
Weaken if cost sensitivity removes most of the advantage.
suggested_validation: Predefine the ETF universe before running.
Use one ranking lookback and top-N count before seeing results.
Run walk-forward validation before interpreting any in-sample advantage.
references: Academic and practitioner literature on cross-sectional momentum
Practitioner research on ETF relative-strength rotation
